rationale: A wins because it refuses the shiny but unsupported story. Its price angle says, “the fact block pairs the two but never connects them,” which is exactly the discipline this update needs. B opens with “Chipotle bets a robot can hold the line on menu prices,” then admits the labor-cost offset is unproven; that is the pitch equivalent of stepping on the rake and labeling it strategy.
gaps_in_A: “Food robotics has been stuck in pilot-program purgatory” is plausible beat context, but it is not in the supplied update and needs sourcing or a hedge.
“100 stores is the pilot-to-deployment threshold this beat watches for” asserts an industry threshold without proof. Good instinct, but don't invent the beat's magic number.
gaps_in_B: “Chipotle bets a robot can hold the line on menu prices” invents a causal link between Autocado and flat prices that the update does not support.
“with automation as the implied offset” is the central grounding failure. The update explicitly says labor-cost figures are not disclosed.
“The pricing angle is strongest only if you can disclose or credibly source the labor-cost offset” is useful, but it also proves the headline is not ready to pitch as written.
“Inside the kitchen where a robot halved the time it takes to make guac” implies reporter access or a scene piece before access is secured. Keep it as an operations angle, not a pretend ride-along.
